why_this_file_exists: ID-05's second clause forbids a cast that hides a genuine type error, and a
green typecheck is not evidence about that: `tsc` has no flag for `no as
never`. This baseline is what turns the count into a RATCHET: `pnpm typecheck`
fails if the number of non-test `as never` casts GROWS.
WHY A BASELINE AND NOT ZERO. The V1 case FAILed on this clause with 475
occurrences. Sweeping them is per-site review, not a mechanical edit: measured
on this tree, two instances of the SAME syntactic shape behave differently --
removing both casts from `ctx.plugin(storageJsonPlugin as never, { root } as
never)` compiles clean, while removing only the config cast from
`ctx.plugin(Storage, {} as never)` reports TS2345. A gate that demanded zero
today would be a gate nobody could pass honestly. A gate that forbids GROWTH is
enforceable now and is the property that stops the hole widening.

THE THIRD REMOVAL IS THE ONE THIS FILE HAD CALLED UNFIXABLE. Its own entry read
`MASK -- REPORTED, NOT FIXED` for `durability-runner.ts:93`, and deferred the fix
as 'a topology change to a crash rig whose child is SIGKILLed mid-run'. That
estimate was too pessimistic. Mounting the real AgentLoop is two lines, exactly as
the sibling rigs do (`concurrency.test.ts:151`):
await mountAgentLoopTestDependencies(ctx)
await ctx.plugin(AgentLoop, { agents: [] })
const rootAgent = await ctx.agentLoop.create(SessionId('root-session'), {...})
and then `createRun` receives a real `Agent`, so the fabricated
`{ session: { header: { id } } } as never` literal is deleted rather than
justified. The crash semantics are untouched: the rig still SIGKILLs the child
mid-run and observes only what reached disk. Mounting more services changes WHAT
the child can do, not WHEN it dies.
MEASURED: `node helpers/typecheck.mjs` -> `1 non-test cast(s); baseline allows 1`,
`typecheck: PASS`. The durability-advanced suite is 33/33.
THE LESSON WORTH KEEPING: 'not fixable at the type level' was true and still did
not mean 'not fixable'. The cast was hiding a real error, and the honest fix was
not to change the type but to give the rig a real object of that type. A baseline
entry that says a fix is out of scope should say WHAT would be in scope, which this
one did -- and the thing it named turned out to cost two lines.

argument that the cast documented an intent: the probe reads a tool name
deliberately outside the typed tool catalog, because `v4_target` is registered
at runtime. The argument for KEEPING it does not survive its own measurement.
A cast that changes nothing -- removing it compiles clean, as this entry's own
`revealed_error` records -- is not documenting a type fact, it is decorating a
line. The intent is carried by the probe's prose, which is where a reader looks
for it, and by the neighbouring comment about the registry.
So it was removed and the ratchet was lowered to 2. The general rule this

the cast is noise -- that is what separates it from the durability-runner entry
above. The diagnostic is about the PROBE's own fabricated object, not about the

model-facing tool against a hand-built context carrying exactly the two members

The alternative -- mounting the real composition -- is what the OTHER arms do;

suppressed product error, which is the distinction ID-05's clause is about.

how_to_add_a_justified_cast: 1. Add an entry here with file, line, the verdict, the error that removing it
reveals (or `none`), and why it is not a mask.
2. Raise `non_test_as_never_count` by one IN THE SAME COMMIT, so the
justification and the permission are reviewed together.
3. `pnpm typecheck` then passes. A cast added WITHOUT this edit fails the gate.
NEVER `as any`, and never an inline `@ts-ignore`: the point of the ratchet is
that the cast stays VISIBLE and REVIEWED.
